system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
On the grid below, draw the reflection of the shape in the dotted line of symmetry.

[Image: Grid with a polygon and a dashed line of symmetry]

Figure, described in words:
An 8 by 8 grid of square cells with a vertical dashed line of symmetry running along the central vertical grid line (between the 4th and 5th columns from the left).
To the right of the dashed line is a six-sided polygon with vertices at grid intersections (with column lines 0 to 8 from left to right, and row lines 0 to 8 from top to bottom):
- (column 4, row 3) on the dashed line
- (column 5, row 2)
- (column 6, row 4)
- (column 7, row 4)
- (column 7, row 6)
- (column 4, row 5) on the dashed line

The edges of the polygon connect these vertices in sequence:
- A straight segment from (4, 3) up and right to (5, 2)
- A segment from (5, 2) down and right to (6, 4)
- A horizontal segment from (6, 4) to (7, 4)
- A vertical segment from (7, 4) down to (7, 6)
- A slanted segment from (7, 6) up and left to (4, 5)
- A vertical segment of length 2 along the dashed line from (4, 5) up to (4, 3)

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Reflect each vertex across the vertical dashed line (the line between columns 4 and 5, i.e., x = 4) and join them in the same order. The two vertices on the dashed line stay where they are: (4,3) and (4,5). The other four map as follows: (5,2) goes to (3,2), (6,4) goes to (2,4), (7,4) goes to (1,4), and (7,6) goes to (1,6). On the grid, draw the mirror-image shape to the left of the dashed line with these edges: a straight segment from (4,3) down-left... more precisely up and left to (3,2); a segment from (3,2) down and left to (2,4); a horizontal segment from (2,4) to (1,4); a vertical segment from (1,4) down to (1,6); a slanted segment from (1,6) to (4,5); and the vertical segment of length 2 along the dashed line from (4,5) back up to (4,3). The result is a six-sided shape that is the mirror image of the original shape on the left side of the dashed line.

llm_thinking: I need to reflect the polygon across the vertical dashed line at x=4, applying x → 8-x to each vertex: (4,3), (5,2), (6,4), (7,4), (7,6), (4,5) map to (4,3), (3,2), (2,4), (1,4), (1,6), (4,5), giving the mirrored shape on the left side of the line.
